rapport_notes: Friendly and transparent; proactively caught that the customer's online quote was tied to a branch without availability and fixed it rather than letting the customer discover it later.

evidence_quotes.agenda: 'do you have any just off the top concerns or questions I can answer right at the gate?' — asked right after basic contact info, before address/date/items were probed.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — the customer said 'No, not really,' just explaining he'd started an online quote; no concern was raised to dig into.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: 'you only pay for the time you use so if you use less than the two and a half... that's what you would end up paying for' (beats-it-pay-less).

top_strength: Caught that the customer's self-entered online quote was tied to a branch with no availability and a $190 trip fee, then proactively found a same-week date at the correct branch to save him the money — real advocacy, not just order-taking.
coaching_note: None of the four differentiators (damage coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, communication plan) were mentioned anywhere in the call, and there was no explicit close — the call ended with the customer needing to check with his wife. Working in even one or two of the 'few reminders' lines before the close could have helped seal it on this call.
